content:
Last month we ran a poll, and the vast majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should exit the advertising business.

Ads have now landed in Apple Maps in the US and Canada, and I think it's about as distasteful as you'd expect…

Apple previewed this back in March, telling us ads would start appearing in the Maps app at some point this summer. We got our first look at what the ads actually look like yesterday, and Apple confirmed they have been rolling out over the past few days. All users in the US and Canada will see them in the coming weeks.

  • Before search: Sponsored suggestions appear in the Featured Places column on the search page.
  • After search: Ads appear alongside the relevant search results.

Apple says privacy is one of the priorities.

I believe that, but I still find the whole thing pretty tacky for two reasons.

Top comment by John Atkinson:

The only reason I can think of that isn't about ad revenue is that adding ads to Apple Maps might encourage more businesses to claim their listings. Apple Maps has always lagged behind Google Maps, and one of the longstanding reasons for that is that many businesses simply can't be bothered to add themselves to the map, or let their listings go stale. In North America this isn't a huge problem because of iPhone penetration, but overseas it absolutely is.

In theory, ads could be the carrot that gets businesses to upload their info, because they could run ads in the same app (or, in order to run ads, their marketing team would fill in all the details). I don't really believe this is why Apple is doing it? Absolutely not — clearly it's to make more money — but at least there's the side benefit of improving map data quality.

First, while Apple won't serve you personalised ads via any kind of tracking, almost every other app and website does. Most people will naturally assume the iPhone maker does too — however unfair that perception — and this will damage the company's reputation for protecting user privacy.

Second, it's tacky. Advertising is a necessary evil in the app and online publishing ecosystem: it's how free apps or sites are able to keep the lights on. But Apple absolutely does not need to chase ad revenue to pay the rent: it already charges a hefty premium for its top-tier hardware. Ads simply don't fit the brand.

I remember John Gruber once likened ads in Apple apps to those horrible Intel Inside stickers on cheap Windows laptops. Of course we understand that companies making cheap laptops need to chase every possible revenue stream, but we'd never expect Apple to slap the same sticker on a MacBook and cheapen the brand. So how can we accept ads in native apps on Apple devices?

My position remains the same: Apple simply shouldn't be in the advertising business.
